question: Does God listen to and answer prayers?
summary: Proverbs 2:3-5, Proverbs 8:17, and Matthew 7:8 / Luke 11:9-10 promise that anyone who seeks God will find him — ask and receive, knock and the door opens. Psalm 18:41, Proverbs 1:28, Lamentations 3:8 and 3:44, and Luke 13:24 directly contradict this: God refuses to answer, shuts out prayer, hides behind a cloud, and tells seekers they will not be able to enter. The contradiction is canonical, intra-testamental, and even intra-Proverbial.

reconcile.connective: Gill reads the psalm's unanswered cry, like the Proverbs warning, as God's retaliation against enemies — not a broken promise to sincere seekers.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible catalogs this exact clash as "Can God be found?", setting the seek-and-find promises flatly against the seek-and-not-find refusals.

pd_work.resource: John Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874), 'Doctrinal Discrepancies,' pp. 70-72
pd_work.author: John Haley
pd_work.note: Haley treats this exact cluster under three paired headings — 'Inaccessibility' (Ps 145:18/Jas 4:8 vs. Lam 3:44), 'All seekers find. Some do not find' (Matt 7:8 vs. Luke 13:24 and John 7:34), and 'Early seekers successful. Some fail to find' (Prov 8:17 vs. Prov 1:28, quoted verbatim) — arguing each pair addresses a different class of seeker (timing, sincerity, penitence), not a real collision. Verified via full-text search of the archive.org djvu.txt scan.

link.title: GotQuestions: Are there any conditions to answered prayer?
link.note: live apologetic treatment arguing the prayer promises are conditioned on faith, righteousness, and God's will, not unconditional — the same qualifying move Haley applies to Prov 1:28/8:17 (does not cite this row's specific verses).

excerpts.attribution: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63)
excerpts.excerpt_text: …even unto the Lord, but he answered them not; as Saul, for instance, Sa1 28:6; so God deals with wicked men, often by way of righteous retaliation; see Pro 1:28.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Cross-references Proverbs 1:28's 'I will not answer' to explain Psalm 18:41's unanswered cry as retributive justice against the impenitent/wicked, distinguishing them from the sincere seekers promised an answer in Prov 8:17 and Matt 7:8.
excerpts.source_note_text:
They cried, but there was none to save them,.... It is in Sa2 22:42; "they looked"; that is, they looked round about, here and there, to see if there were any near at hand to help and deliver them; they cried in their distress, and because of the anguish of their spirits, and for help and assistance, but in vain; they cried, as Jarchi thinks, to their idols, as Jonah's mariners cried everyone to their god; and, if so, it is no wonder there was none to save; for such are gods that cannot save: but it follows,
even unto the Lord, but he answered them not; as Saul, for instance, Sa1 28:6; so God deals with wicked men, often by way of righteous retaliation; see Pro 1:28.
